payload.prompt:
A realistic, continuous 15-second video of a young Asian woman writing and annotating text on a transparent glass writing board against a matte black background.

The woman wears a plain black T-shirt and blue jeans. She holds a bright neon-yellow marker in her right hand. The camera is fixed, medium-wide shot, straight-on perspective, professional studio lighting. The board is completely blank at the start. The glass is perfectly clear with no reflection of her, no mirrored double, no ghost image, and no second figure visible anywhere in or behind the glass -- only one woman is ever visible in the frame, at the center, and the area behind and beside the glass is plain matte black with nothing else in it.

She writes exactly five short lines of text, top to bottom, left-aligned, stacked with generous blank space between them, in small, compact handwriting that stays on a single horizontal line each -- never wrapping to a second line:
1. "I vibe-coded my app"
2. "in a weekend."
3. "Launched 19."
4. "So this week I pay"
5. "$99 on x.country"
Each line's text is reproduced exactly as written above, character for character, with no extra punctuation added anywhere -- no parentheses, no extra periods, no extra dashes, no stray marks of any kind next to or after any word. "$99" is written as a dollar sign followed directly by the two digits "9" and "9" with no period or space between them. "x.country" is written with a period between "x" and "country", never a hyphen or dash.

Writing sequence, in this exact order:

1. She looks at the board, raises her hand, and begins writing line 1 at the top-left. The yellow ink appears progressively, exactly underneath the moving marker tip, one letter at a time, never ahead of the tip, never appearing all at once.
2. She lifts the marker, moves down to the start of line 2, and writes it the same way, directly below line 1.
3. She continues the same way for line 3, then line 4, then line 5, each one appearing directly below the previous line, in the same handwriting size and style, never retracing or repeating any word from a previous line. The instant each line of text is finished, the marker lifts immediately -- no extra mark, no stray punctuation, no small tick or loop is added next to or after the last word of any line.
4. Once all five lines are completely written, she lifts the marker and draws a closed yellow rectangle around the word "vibe-coded" only, in line 1 -- tightly enclosing just that one hyphenated word, not touching "I", not touching "my app". The rectangle is drawn as four straight strokes, one side at a time, each growing progressively under the moving tip, the same way the letters did -- it does not appear all at once.
5. She lifts the marker and draws a closed yellow oval/circle around the text "$99" only, in line 5 -- tightly enclosing just those three characters, not touching or enclosing any other word, not touching "on x.country". The circle is drawn as one continuous curved stroke, growing progressively under the moving tip -- it does not appear all at once.
6. She lifts the marker again and draws one straight horizontal yellow line directly underneath the text "x.country" only, in line 5. The underline starts exactly below the left edge of the "x" in "x.country" and ends exactly below the right edge of the final "y" in "x.country" -- its left end must be clearly to the right of the circle drawn around "$99", with a visible gap between the circle and the start of the underline, and its length must match only the word "x.country", not the word "on", not "$99", and not any empty space. This line also grows progressively under the moving tip, from its left end to its right end.
7. The instant each stroke (every letter, the rectangle, the circle, and the underline) reaches its natural endpoint, the marker lifts immediately -- no extra tick mark, no small correction stroke, no double-back, no wiggle, no decorative mark of any kind is left behind, anywhere on the board.
8. She lifts the marker, lowers her hand, and looks toward the camera. The finished board -- five lines of text, a rectangle around "vibe-coded", a circle around "$99", and an underline below "x.country" -- remains visible and completely unchanged.

Critical physical and temporal consistency requirements:

- Every mark (letter, rectangle, circle, and underline) is created by actual physical contact between the marker tip and the glass.
- The marker tip and the growing end of every stroke stay perfectly synchronized, frame by frame, for the entire video -- text, rectangle, circle, and underline alike.
- No stroke may appear before the marker reaches its location, and no stroke may appear instantly or partially formed before the tip draws it.
- The rectangle, circle, and underline are plain marks with no arrowhead, no decorative flourish, and no extra ink beyond their stated shape.
- Previously written text and previously drawn marks stay perfectly stationary and visually identical throughout -- never redrawn, never shifted, never altered, never erased, never faded out, and never replaced by different wording or different capitalization. Once a line of text or a mark has been drawn, it remains on the board, unchanged, pixel for pixel, for the rest of the video -- including during and after every later stroke.
- Her face, age, and features do not change from the start of the clip to the end -- the exact same person throughout.
- The marker stays firmly and naturally gripped between her fingers; her wrist, fingers, elbow, and arm move with realistic human anatomy.
- She looks at the board and the marker tip the entire time she is writing or drawing, and only looks toward the camera at the very end, after everything is finished.
- There is exactly one woman in the frame throughout the entire video -- no reflection, no mirrored copy, no second person, no ghosting of any kind, at any point, anywhere in the frame.
- No camera cuts, zooms, transitions, time-lapses, or editing tricks.
- Consistent line thickness, neon-yellow color, and sharp edges throughout.
- Natural hand speed with brief pauses between strokes.

Photorealistic, single continuous take, 30 fps, high temporal consistency, realistic marker-to-surface interaction, crisp handwriting and geometric marks, no animation overlays, no post-production drawing or text effects.
